clue.text: Town with young female in' charge

parts.note: a maiden is a girl or unmarried young woman
the head is the person in charge, as of a school

explanation.surface: A town run by a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe after 'in' is a printing blemish. MAIDENHEAD is a town in Berkshire, west of London, on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidenhead is a Berkshire riverside settlement, so 'town' is a plain example definition.

clue.text: Bill's down in the mouth — a bird responsible for that

indicators.note: the bill letters sit inside the word for a mouth

parts.note: a maw is an animal's mouth or gullet

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'down' means the letters for bill are written from the bottom upward

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A parrot with a drooping beak is blamed for its sad look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like the bird's beak, which the surface plays on; it is an account, and 'down' turns it upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaw is a large long-tailed tropical parrot with a huge hooked beak.

clue.text: International airmen ringing up Italian girlfriend

indicators.note: ringing means surrounding, so the airmen's letters form a ring around the rest

parts.note: IATA, the International Air Transport Association, is the airlines' trade body

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'up' means the Italian's letters are written bottom to top

parts.note: a Roman is an Italian, a native of Rome

explanation.surface: Foreign pilots phone their sweetheart in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing up' looks like one phrase meaning telephoning; it splits into 'ringing' (surrounding) and 'up' (turning the Italian upward).
explanation.definitionFit: Inamorata is an Italian-derived word for a woman one is in love with, a sweetheart or mistress.

clue.text: A token of friendly relations in a battlefield?

explanation.definitionFit: The ring given at betrothal is a token of a pledged relationship, and a field where battle is joined is jokingly a ring for an armed engagement.

clue.text: Shelter and support turned up in time

indicators.note: the support's letters are placed inside the word for a time

parts.note: an hour is a period of time

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'turned up' means the support's letters are written upward

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: Someone offers refuge and backing just when needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like 'arrived'; here it turns the undergarment upward before it goes inside the time.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour is to give refuge to, as a port gives ships safe haven.

clue.text: The sort of letters a couple of animals produce

parts.note: a nag (an old horse) and a ram (a male sheep) are two beasts
a nag (an old horse) and a ram (a male sheep) are two beasts

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what two beasts might write if they could spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters A, NAG and RAM are themselves rearranged-word material, which is the joke: these letters, jumbled, form a word of that very kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A word made by rearranging another's letters is the kind of letter group meant.

clue.text: Animal about to run here

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the animal is read from end to start

parts.note: the wolf is a wild canine animal

explanation.surface: A beast is poised to bolt from this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to run' looks like 'ready to run'; 'about' instead reverses WOLF.
explanation.definitionFit: To flow is to run, as water or a stream runs.

clue.text: Stand-in circumnavigator missed a bearing

indicators.note: missed means went without, so a letter is dropped from the sailor's name

parts.note: Joshua Slocum was the first person to sail alone around the world
S, south, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A substitute sailor went round the world without a compass point.
explanation.walkthrough: The circumnavigator is Joshua Slocum (1844-1909), first solo sailor round the globe; drop S (south) from his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric covering temporarily for another, a deputy.

clue.text: A ferry was organised for travellers

indicators.note: organised means arranged into order, so these letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A ferry crossing has been laid on for passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: Wayfarers are people who journey, especially on foot.

clue.text: Governor of Bengal responsible for two conflicts outside the central arena

indicators.note: outside means the two conflicts stand on either side of the arena's centre

parts.note: a war is a conflict, and Hastings, fought in 1066, is a famous battle
a war is a conflict, and Hastings, fought in 1066, is a famous battle

indicators.note: central means only the middle letters of the word arena are used

explanation.surface: A colonial ruler started two wars beyond the amphitheatre's core.
explanation.walkthrough: The second conflict is the Battle of Hastings (1066), fought near the English south coast town of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal, impeached in a famous trial.

clue.text: Horse needs a plate

explanation.surface: A horse needs a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A charger is a warhorse ridden into battle, and also a large flat serving dish.

clue.text: Finished in some disorder

indicators.note: the finished letters go inside the word for some

parts.note: any means some, as in 'have you any?'
arch, like finished, can mean consummate or accomplished, as in an arch rogue

explanation.surface: Things ended up in a bit of a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finished' looks like 'ended'; here it is an adjective meaning consummate, as in an arch-villain.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchy is lawless chaos, a state without rule or order.

clue.text: Shaking Roger down, he could end up in 17

indicators.note: shaking jumbles the letters of the two words, rearranging them

explanation.surface: Roughing up Roger lands a man in a prison work crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is CHAIN GANG, where a convicted offender might end up.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal or offender might be sentenced to a convict work gang.

clue.text: A measure of spirit Jack knocked back

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

indicators.note: knocked back means turned backwards, so the sailor's letters are reversed

parts.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, an AB (able seaman)

explanation.surface: A sailor downed a tot of liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' suggests drinking; it reverses AB. 'Measure' is an old word for a dance, with a stately tread.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance can be called a measure, and the rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Crowd took a dip in the river? On the contrary

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
on the contrary says to swap the containing roles, so the river goes inside the dip

parts.note: swam means bathed, took a dip

explanation.surface: A mob went bathing in a stream, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, SWAM would go in R; 'On the contrary' flips it so R goes inside SWAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a large thronging mass, of people or insects.

clue.text: Boat going round port — note, it mustn't be criticised

indicators.note: going round means the boat's letters surround the rest

parts.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed boat
Acre is an ancient port in northern Israel
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: A vessel rounds a harbour while a memo warns against complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: The port is Acre in northern Israel, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred cow is an institution or idea held to be above question.

clue.text: Feature with high bridge girl loves in a city

indicators.note: the girl and the loves go inside the city

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital city
Ann is a girl's name
love is zero in tennis scoring, written O, so two loves are Os

explanation.surface: A girl in a romantic city admires someone's profile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high bridge' suggests a span; it is the bridge of the nose, high in an aquiline profile.
explanation.definitionFit: This facial shape has a prominent, high-ridged bridge, as on classical busts.

clue.text: Where to see some footballers flying

explanation.definitionFit: Wide forwards play out on the flanks of the pitch, and a bird in flight is airborne.

clue.text: Punishment changing a crook

indicators.note: crook as an adjective means bent or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A villain's sentence is being altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a criminal, which fits the surface; it signals the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Being chained to fellow convicts for hard labour was a penal sentence.

clue.text: When I head a movement, it's from the east

indicators.note: in a down entry, to head is to sit above, so the I comes before the rest

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I arrived'
a tic is an involuntary twitch or movement

explanation.surface: Someone leading a political movement claims eastern origins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head a movement' suggests leadership; 'head' just puts I above A TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Asiatic means of Asia, the continent to the east of Europe.

clue.text: Hanging around the east, a malevolent spirit

indicators.note: the spirit's letters are placed around the compass point

parts.note: a goblin is a mischievous or wicked sprite
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A wicked sprite hovers near the eastern side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanging around' looks like loitering; 'Hanging' is the definition, a tapestry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gobelin is a tapestry woven at the Paris Gobelins works, used as a wall covering.

clue.text: Those who are against decapitating 'an insect

indicators.note: decapitating means removing the head, so the first letter of the insect goes

parts.note: the mantis is a predatory insect

explanation.surface: Protesters are beheading a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe before 'an' is a printing blemish. Remove the M heading MANTIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Antis are opponents, people who oppose a policy or proposal.

clue.text: More mature tree

explanation.definitionFit: Older people are senior in years, and the elder is a shrub or small tree bearing flowers and berries.

clue.text: Initial appearance of foreign objection

parts.note: de is French for of, so 'of' in a foreign language
'but' introduces an objection, as in 'no buts'

explanation.surface: A newcomer's first showing draws an overseas complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A debut is someone's first public performance.

clue.text: Intermediary, I suppose, is keeping note in Latin and in French

indicators.note: is keeping means holding inside, so the phrase for supposing goes round the note and the French word

parts.note: ween is an archaic verb meaning suppose or think, so I ween
NB stands for nota bene, Latin for note well
et is French for and

explanation.surface: A go-between muses on a jotting written in two languages.
explanation.walkthrough: Ween is an archaic verb for suppose; nota bene is Latin for 'note well'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something halfway is intermediate, occupying a middle position.

clue.text: Popular rising overrunning Ger-man-republic

indicators.note: in a down entry, overrunning means lying over the next piece
in a down entry, rising means the popular letters are read upward

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
Ger is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A popular uprising sweeps across a German state.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'German-republic' is a line-break artefact. IN reversed by 'rising' gives NI, placed above GER.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked West African state governed as a republic.

clue.text: The government press

explanation.surface: The government press.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior ministers form the ruling council, and a press is a cupboard, as is this piece of furniture.

clue.text: Cutting school

explanation.surface: Skipping school.
explanation.definitionFit: Slicing open with a blade is cutting, and Lancing College is an English independent boarding school in West Sussex.

clue.text: Pardon? said man of power

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word sounds like the written entry

parts.note: 'what?' is a way of saying pardon, asking for repetition

explanation.surface: A powerful man asks someone to repeat themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: James Watt was the Scottish engineer of steam engines; the unit of power is named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: The engineer behind the steam engine gave his name to the unit of power.

clue.text: It makes topping cigar, using a good mixture

indicators.note: a good mixture means the letters are thoroughly mixed up

explanation.surface: A smoker is advised to blend a cigar well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' sounds like excellent, but it is a cake topping.
explanation.definitionFit: Powdered sugar is used to make the sweet coating on cakes.
